title: What Binary Is This: Which Compiler, How Optimised, What Sanitizer, and Which Numbers May Be Compared

questions.question: A loop is timed at 300 microseconds on a laptop and 40 on the robot, running the same source. What is the most likely difference?
options: The build: a debug build, assertions on and no optimisation, can be several times slower than a release build of the same code
questions.explanation: Nothing in the program says which kind of build it is.

questions.question: Why does current_build check for clang before gcc?
options: Clang also defines __GNUC__, so testing gcc first would call a clang build gcc
questions.explanation: Clang defines the macros of the compiler it imitates.

questions.question: The suite's sanitizer build described itself as gcc-11 c++17 debug address 64bit little. How was address found?
options: Through the compiler's macro __SANITIZE_ADDRESS__ in gcc, or __has_feature in clang

questions.question: Which of these pairs of builds are comparable for speed?
options: A release build and an address sanitizer build of the same compiler
Two release builds with the same compiler, version and pointer width, with no sanitizer on either
A debug build and a release build
Any two on the same machine
questions.explanation: Even the same sanitizer build compared with itself is not a speed to trust.

questions.question: A report line has a double space in it. What does parse_build do?
options: Refuses it, because the pieces are split at single spaces and an empty piece is how a malformed line is noticed, and leaves the output alone
questions.explanation: All 12 malformed lines in the suite were refused.

questions.question: Two builds both read gcc-11 c++17 release none 64bit little. What can still differ?
options: The optimisation level (-O1 and -O3 are both release), the warning flags, the standard library and the machine
questions.explanation: The line records what the macros say, not the flags that were given.
